closure.title: Closure-challenge benchmark
closure.our_entry: Entry of record (round 5, 2026-08-07) scored 0.0566 overall through the benchmark's own unmodified harness across six pre-registered scoring calls (RANS-identity floor, round-1 periodic-hills correction, round-2 extended to ducts and NASA hump, round-3 test-blind decline-gate, round-4 Reynolds-invariant duct rescale, round-5 untrained QCR2000 forward solve on the ducts). Rank 1 of 7 scored locally against the LIVE public board fetched 2026-08-11T23:33Z, which carries six entries and a new leader (Yang, 0.0580); our own scoring is done at the frozen benchmark commit deb91557, which scores but does not rank. A local scoring, not an official placement. P(rank 1) = 50%: a case-level bootstrap over the eight scored cases puts the probability that this ordering survives a comparable set of cases at 50%, and an eight-case sample cannot pin that tighter than 0-97% at 95%. The previous figure - P(rank 1) = 68%, 2-100% at 95% - is STRUCK as of 2026-08-11: it was computed against a FOUR-entry board that no longer exists, and our margin over Yang more than halved with the change, 0.002878 to 0.001365. Best result on the public board on four of the eight test cases - but two of those four (alpha_05_4071_4048, alpha_05_4071_2024) are the organisers' own unmodified RANS field, which our decline gate passed through untouched; the credit there belongs to the baseline every entrant is handed for free, not to our model, and anyone submitting it unchanged scores exactly the same. THAT COUNT IS SUPERSEDED AS OF 2026-08-11 and is kept only so the correction is visible: it was measured against the FOUR-entry board. Against the live six-entry board the count is TWO of the eight, both alpha_15 hills having been lost to Tian, Buchanan, Hickel and Dwight - and the two that survive are exactly the two organisers' baseline rows, so the count belonging to our own model is ZERO of eight. Our model is best on no single case. The overall is a mean and not a count of wins, so 0.0566 is still the lowest number on the board; this entry wins on consistency, not on peaks, and that is the honest description of it. Not yet submitted to the benchmark's steward. The lead is not statistically decided against any of the four entries nearest us: the 0.001365 margin over Yang sits against a per-case spread fifteen times larger (t = -0.19, four of eight cases won), so on a different set of eight cases the ordering could reverse, and the same is true of Reissmann (t = -0.50), Wu and Zhang (t = -0.95) and Tian, Buchanan, Hickel and Dwight (t = -1.03); the margins over Liu and Montoya do survive that test. The standing is three deletions wide - drop any one of alpha_15_13929_4048, alpha_15_13929_2024 or alpha_05_4071_4048 and the point rank falls to 2, 3 and 2. AR_1_Ret_360 and AR_3_Ret_360 are ties below the precision the board publishes to, and are not per-case wins. Source: campaign/PROBABILITY_OF_RANK_SIX_ENTRY_2026-08-11.md; the superseded four-entry computation is kept at campaign/PROBABILITY_OF_RANK_2026-08-10.md.

fleet_learning.title: Learning from the fleet ledger
fleet_learning.summary: Distilled from 208067 rows of the mega-batch ledger (207979 completed evaluations); every relationship carries measured fit quality, never assertion.
highlights: Across 69115 wing polars, higher aspect ratio raises L/D: about +1.90 in L/D per unit of aspect ratio, and the fit explains 93 percent of the variance (r2 = 0.93). That is a strong relationship, measured, not assumed.
The induced-drag rows imply a span efficiency near 1.02 (spread 0.02 over 69115 polars), pulled straight from cl and cdi.
Best wing seen so far: L/D 47.2 at aspect ratio 16.0 and sweep 13.6 deg (ledger row 145432).
Over 69194 cylinder solves in the steady-laminar band, Cd falls with Re with a log-log slope of -0.43 (r2 = 1.00), consistent with laminar drag theory.
100 percent of the 69194 cylinder solves converged to residual tolerance.
Across 68996 reduced-order valve evaluations, wider opening angles cut cycle-weighted loss (slope -148.5 Pa per degree, r2 = 0.76); the lowest loss seen is 1267 Pa at 85.0 deg (ledger row 109319).
Reliability: 88 of 208067 attempted evaluations failed (0 percent); every failure stays in the ledger and counts against the fleet.
All of the above rests on 207979 completed evaluations in the fleet ledger; nothing here is asserted without a row behind it.

challenges.title: NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource verification cases
challenges.host: NASA Langley / Turbulence Model Benchmarking Working Group
challenges.what: the reference verification cases, including the 2D flat plate and bump-in-channel, that a RANS code must reproduce on refined grids
challenges.status: flat plate measured, bump not conclusive
challenges.entry: flat plate now on a 5-grid ladder to 208,896 cells and bump on 3, against the published CFL3D values: flat-plate Cd 0.0028636 vs 0.0028533 at matched grid size, bump Cd 0.003567 vs 0.003607. The flat plate's finest triple is the first ladder here to earn a reportable discretization band, 4.244e-6 or 0.148% of the value, at observed order 1.634; that order is still rising rung on rung, so the band is earned and the asymptotic range is not claimed. The two halves do not stand equally and the bump number carries its status: none of its three rungs prints the solver's own convergence statement, its observed order is 0.52 with the pressure component non-monotone, and the discretization certifier refuses the triplet, so that 1.1% agreement is a comparison and not a converged result. NACA 0012 airfoil next

credentials.name: sphere
credentials.reason:
measured C_d 0.095 matches the supercritical (post-drag-crisis) regime (C_d ~0.09, Achenbach 1972 (supercritical branch, Cd ~ 0.07-0.10)), not the subcritical (laminar separation, wide wake) reference C_d 0.47; steady fully-turbulent RANS delays boundary-layer separation and reproduces the post-drag-crisis wake, so the coefficient reads supercritical even when the solve Reynolds number is subcritical
; no like-for-like comparison available
credentials.source: Achenbach 1972, J. Fluid Mech. 54:565; consistent with Schlichting, Boundary-Layer Theory
